title: imap: OBJECTID extension (RFC 8474) — map IPFS CIDs to EmailID/ThreadID
description:
Implement RFC 8474 OBJECTID, which provides stable EmailID and ThreadID values per message.

This extension is architecturally natural for usenet-ipfs: articles are content-addressed by CID, which is already a permanent, globally unique, content-derived identifier. The CID maps directly to RFC 8474 EmailID with no additional storage.

What:
- Advertise OBJECTID in CAPABILITY.
- Return X-GM-MSGID-style EMAILID and THREADID in FETCH responses when requested.
- EmailID: the article's IPFS CID (base32-encoded to satisfy the RFC 8474 objectid syntax, which requires a letter prefix and only URL-safe chars).
- ThreadID: derive from the article's References/In-Reply-To chain; group articles in the same thread under one stable ThreadID. Can be the CID of the earliest known ancestor in the thread.
- Clients that support OBJECTID (Thunderbird) use it for efficient sync and deduplication across folder copies.

Note: because CIDs are content-derived, two copies of the same article in different folders will have the same EmailID, which is correct per RFC 8474 §5.
notes: BLOCKED: RFC 8474 OBJECTID adds StatusDataItemName::EmailId and StatusDataItemName::ThreadId, neither of which exist in imap-types 2.0.0-alpha.6. Additionally, meaningful OBJECTID response requires article IPFS CIDs which are not yet wired to the reader server.
